title.zh: 卷41 列傳第33 王襃 庾信
title.en: Volume 41 Biographies 33: Wang Bao; Yu Xin
title.raw: 卷41 列傳第33 王襃 庾信 Volume 41 Biographies 33: Wang Bao; Yu Xin

sentences.zh: 王襃 庾信

translations.literal: Wang Bao; Yu Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao; Yu Xin.

sentences.zh: 王襃字子淵，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Bao, courtesy name Ziyuan, was a native of Linyi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao, styled Ziyuan, came from Linyi in Langya.

sentences.zh: 曾祖儉，齊侍中、太尉、南昌文憲公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jian was Qi Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Commandant, and Duke Wenxian of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jian had served Qi as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commandant and was posthumously titled Duke Wenxian of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 祖騫，梁侍中、金紫光祿大夫、南昌安侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qian was Liang Attendant-in-Ordinary, Household Counsellor with Golden Bells and Purple Pendants, and Marquis An of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qian had been Liang Attendant-in-Ordinary, Household Counsellor with Golden Bells and Purple Pendants, and Marquis An of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 父規，梁侍中、左民尚書、南昌章侯。

translations.literal: His father Gui was Liang Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of the Left for the People, and Marquis Zhang of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui had been Liang Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of the Left for the People, and Marquis Zhang of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 竝有重名於江左。

translations.literal: All alike enjoyed great renown south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: They all enjoyed great renown south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 襃識量淵通，志懷沉靜。

translations.literal: Bao's discernment and capacity were profound and penetrating; his will and mind were deep and calm.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was profoundly discerning and inwardly steady of purpose.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，善談笑，博覽史傳，尤工屬文。

translations.literal: He had fine bearing and deportment, was skilled in witty conversation, and read widely in history and tradition; he was especially accomplished at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome in bearing, skilled in conversation, widely read in history, and especially accomplished as a writer.

sentences.zh: 梁國子祭酒蕭子雲，襃之姑夫也，特善草隸。

translations.literal: Xiao Ziyun, Director of the National University of Liang, was Bao's uncle by marriage and was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziyun, Director of the National University under Liang, was married to Bao's aunt and was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 襃少以姻戚，去來其家，遂相模範。

translations.literal: Because of this marriage tie, Bao in his youth often came and went at his house and took him as a model.
translations.idiomatic: In youth, because of the family tie, Bao often visited his household and took him as a model.

sentences.zh: 俄而名亞子雲，竝見重於世。

translations.literal: Before long his fame ranked just below Ziyun's, and both were held in esteem by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his fame stood just below Ziyun's, and both were esteemed in their time.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝喜其才藝，遂以弟鄱陽王恢之女妻之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang delighted in his talent and artistry and therefore gave him in marriage the daughter of his younger brother, Prince Hui of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang delighted in his gifts and gave him in marriage the daughter of his younger brother, Prince Hui of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，轉太子舍人，襲爵南昌縣侯。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretary Gentleman, was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and inherited the marquisate of Nanchang county.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Secretary Gentleman, became Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and inherited the marquisate of Nanchang county.

sentences.zh: 稍遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 宣成王大器，簡文帝之冢嫡，卽襃之姑子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xuan of Cheng, Daqi, was the eldest legitimate son of Emperor Jianwen and thus Bao's cousin on his mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xuan of Cheng, Daqi, was Emperor Jianwen's eldest legitimate son and thus Bao's cousin on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 于時盛選僚佐，乃以襃為文學。

translations.literal: At that time staff were being chosen with great care, and Bao was therefore made Literary Companion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time staff were being chosen with great care, and Bao was appointed Literary Companion.

sentences.zh: 尋遷安成郡守。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to be Administrator of Ancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Administrator of Ancheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 及侯景渡江，建業擾亂，襃輯寧所部，見稱於時。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and Jiankang fell into turmoil, Bao brought his district to order and was praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and Jiankang was thrown into turmoil, Bao brought his district to order and won praise in his time.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制，轉智武將軍、南平內史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the provisional regency, Bao was transferred to General of Sagely Martiality and Interior Administrator of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the provisional regency, Bao was made General of Sagely Martiality and Interior Administrator of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位於江陵，欲待襃以不次之位。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne at Jiangling, he wished to give Bao an extraordinary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne at Jiangling, he wished to give Bao an extraordinary appointment.

sentences.zh: 襃時猶在郡，敕王僧辯以禮發遣。

translations.literal: Bao was still in his commandery, and the emperor ordered Wang Senbian to send for him with full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was still in his commandery, and the emperor ordered Wang Senbian to summon him with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 襃乃將家西上。

translations.literal: Bao then led his household westward.
translations.idiomatic: Bao then led his household westward.

sentences.zh: 元帝與襃有舊，相得甚歡。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan and Bao had an old friendship and got on extremely well.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan and Bao had long been friends and were deeply pleased with each other.

sentences.zh: 拜侍中，累遷吏部尚書、左僕射。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and was promoted in succession to Minister of Personnel and Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and rose in succession to Minister of Personnel and Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 襃旣世冑名家，文學優贍，當時咸相推挹，故旬月之間，位升端右。

translations.literal: Bao, being of a famous hereditary house and richly gifted in letters, was at the time universally pushed forward and esteemed; therefore within the space of a month he rose to the highest offices.
translations.idiomatic: As a man of a great hereditary house and rich literary gifts, Bao was universally pushed forward and esteemed, and within a month he had risen to the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 寵遇日隆，而襃愈自謙虛，不以位地矜人，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Though favor grew daily, Bao became all the more modest and did not lord his rank over others; contemporaries praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Though imperial favor grew daily, Bao became all the more modest and did not lord his rank over others, and his contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 初，元帝平侯景及擒武陵王紀之後，以建業雕殘，方須修復；

translations.literal: Earlier, after Emperor Yuan had pacified Hou Jing and captured Prince Wu of Wuling, Ji, he saw that Jiankang lay in ruins and that repair was urgently needed;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Emperor Yuan had pacified Hou Jing and captured Prince Wu of Wuling, Ji, he saw that Jiankang lay in ruins and that it urgently needed repair;

sentences.zh: 江陵殷盛，便欲安之。

translations.literal: Jiangling was flourishing, and he wished to settle there.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling was flourishing, and he wished to settle the court there.

sentences.zh: 又其故府臣寮，皆楚人也，竝願卽都荊郢。

translations.literal: Moreover, the former members of his staff were all men of Chu and alike wished to make Jing and Ying the capital at once.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, his former staff were all men of Chu and alike wished to make Jing and Ying the capital at once.

sentences.zh: 嘗召羣臣議之。

translations.literal: He once summoned the ministers to discuss the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He once summoned the ministers to discuss the matter.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍胡僧佑、吏部尚書宗懍、太府卿黃羅漢、御史中丞劉鈺等曰：「建業雖是舊都，王氣已盡。

translations.literal: General of the Guards Hu Senyou, Minister of Personnel Zong Lin, Grand Steward Huang Luohan, and Imperial Secretary Liu Yu and others said: "Though Jiankang is the old capital, its royal qi is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guards Hu Senyou, Minister of Personnel Zong Lin, Grand Steward Huang Luohan, Imperial Secretary Liu Yu, and others said: "Though Jiankang is the old capital, its royal qi is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 且與北寇鄰接，止隔一江。

translations.literal: Moreover it borders the northern invaders, with only a single river between.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover it borders the northern invaders, with only one river between.

sentences.zh: 若有不虞，悔無及矣。

translations.literal: If misfortune should come, there will be no remedy.
translations.idiomatic: If misfortune should come, regret will be of no avail.

sentences.zh: 臣等又嘗聞之，荊南之地，有天子氣。

translations.literal: We have also heard that in the lands south of the Jing there is the qi of a Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We have also heard that in the lands south of the Jing there is the qi of a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今陛下龍飛纘業，其應斯乎。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has ascended the dragon throne and continued the enterprise—surely this is the fulfillment?
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has ascended the throne and continued the enterprise—surely this is the fulfillment?

sentences.zh: 天時人事，徵祥如此。

translations.literal: Heaven, the times, and human affairs all show omens such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, the times, and human affairs all show omens such as this.

sentences.zh: 臣等所見，遷徙非宜。

translations.literal: In our view, to move the capital would not be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: In our view, to move the capital would not be fitting.

sentences.zh: 」元帝深以為然。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan deeply agreed.

sentences.zh: 時襃及尚書周弘正咸侍座。

translations.literal: At the time Bao and Minister of the Interior Zhou Hongzheng were both in attendance at his side.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Bao and Minister of the Interior Zhou Hongzheng were both in attendance at his side.

sentences.zh: 乃顧謂襃等曰：「卿意以為何如？

translations.literal: He then turned to Bao and the others and said: "What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to Bao and the others and said: "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」襃性謹慎，知元帝多猜忌，弗敢公言其非。

translations.literal: Bao was by nature cautious and knew that Emperor Yuan was much given to suspicion; he did not dare openly speak against the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was by nature cautious and knew that Emperor Yuan was much given to suspicion; he did not dare openly speak against the plan.

sentences.zh: 當時唯唯而已。

translations.literal: At the time he only assented in vague terms.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he only assented in vague terms.

sentences.zh: 後因清閒密諫，言辭甚切。

translations.literal: Later, in a private moment of leisure, he remonstrated in secret, and his words were very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in a private moment of leisure, he remonstrated in secret, and his words were very earnest.

sentences.zh: 元帝頗納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was quite willing to accept his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was quite willing to accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 然其意好荊、楚，已從僧佑等策。

translations.literal: Yet his heart favored Jing and Chu and he had already followed the plan of Senyou and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his heart favored Jing and Chu and he had already followed the plan of Senyou and the others.

sentences.zh: 明日，乃於衆中謂襃曰：「卿昨日勸還建業，不為無理。

translations.literal: The next day he said before the assembly to Bao: "Your advice yesterday to return to Jiankang was not without reason."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he said before the whole assembly to Bao: "Your advice yesterday to return to Jiankang was not without reason."

sentences.zh: 」襃以宣室之言，豈宜顯之於衆。

translations.literal: Bao felt that words meant for the inner chamber ought not to be displayed before the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Bao felt that words meant for the inner chamber ought not to be displayed before the multitude.

sentences.zh: 知其計之不用也，於是止不復言。

translations.literal: Knowing that his counsel would not be used, he therefore ceased to speak of it further.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that his counsel would not be used, he therefore ceased to speak of it further.

sentences.zh: 及大軍征江陵，元帝授襃都督城西諸軍事。

translations.literal: When the great army marched against Jiangling, Emperor Yuan entrusted Bao with overall command of all military affairs west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army marched against Jiangling, Emperor Yuan entrusted Bao with overall command of all military affairs west of the city.

sentences.zh: 襃本以文雅見知，一旦委以總戎，深自勉勵，盡忠勤之節。

translations.literal: Bao had been known for his literary elegance; now, suddenly entrusted with supreme command, he strove all the more and fulfilled the utmost of loyal diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had been known for literary elegance; now, suddenly entrusted with supreme command, he strove all the more and fulfilled the utmost of loyal diligence.

sentences.zh: 被圍之後，上下猜懼，元帝唯於襃深相委信。

translations.literal: After the siege began, suspicion and fear spread above and below; Emperor Yuan placed deep trust in Bao alone.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege began, suspicion and fear spread above and below; Emperor Yuan placed deep trust in Bao alone.

sentences.zh: 朱買臣率衆出宣陽之西門，與王師戰，買臣大敗。

translations.literal: Zhu Maichen led his troops out through the Xiyang gate of the Xuanyang quarter and fought the royal army; Maichen was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Maichen led his troops out through the Xiyang gate of the Xuanyang quarter and fought the royal army; Maichen was utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 襃督進不能禁，乃貶為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Bao supervised the advance but could not restrain them; he was therefore demoted to General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Bao supervised the advance but could not restrain them; he was therefore demoted to General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 王師攻其外柵，城陷，襃從元帝入子城，猶欲固守。

translations.literal: The royal army assaulted the outer palisade; the city fell, and Bao followed Emperor Yuan into the inner citadel and still wished to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: The royal army assaulted the outer palisade; the city fell, and Bao followed Emperor Yuan into the inner citadel and still wished to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 俄而元帝出降，襃遂與衆俱出。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Yuan went out to surrender, and Bao then came out with the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Yuan went out to surrender, and Bao then came out with the rest.

sentences.zh: 見柱國于謹，謹甚禮之。

translations.literal: He met the pillar of state Yu Jin, who treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He met the pillar of state Yu Jin, who treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 襃曾作《燕歌行》，妙盡關塞寒苦之狀，元帝及諸文士竝和之，而競為淒切之詞。

translations.literal: Bao had once composed "Song of the Yan," brilliantly rendering the bitterness of frontier cold; Emperor Yuan and all the literary men had harmonized with it, each vying in plaintive language.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had once composed "Song of the Yan," brilliantly rendering the bitterness of frontier cold; Emperor Yuan and all the literary men had harmonized with it, each vying in plaintive language.

sentences.zh: 至此方驗焉。

translations.literal: Only now was this truly verified.
translations.idiomatic: Only now was this truly verified.

sentences.zh: 襃與王克、劉穀、宗懍、殷不害等數十人，俱至長安。

translations.literal: Bao, together with Wang Ke, Liu Yi, Zong Lin, Yin Buhai, and several dozen others, all reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Bao, together with Wang Ke, Liu Yi, Zong Lin, Yin Buhai, and several dozen others, all reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜曰：「昔平吳之利，二陸而已。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said with delight: "In the old days the profit of pacifying Wu was no more than the two Lus.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said with delight: "In the old days the profit of pacifying Wu was no more than the two Lus.

sentences.zh: 今定楚之功，羣賢畢至。

translations.literal: Now in settling Chu, all the worthies have come at once.
translations.idiomatic: Now in settling Chu, all the worthies have come at once.

sentences.zh: 可謂過之矣。

translations.literal: One may say this surpasses that."
translations.idiomatic: One may say this surpasses that."

sentences.zh: 」又謂襃及王克曰：「吾卽王氏甥也，卿等竝吾之舅氏。

translations.literal: He also said to Bao and Wang Ke: "I am myself a maternal nephew of the Wang clan; you are all my uncles on that side.
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Bao and Wang Ke: "I am myself a maternal nephew of the Wang clan; you are all my uncles on that side.

sentences.zh: 當以親戚為情，勿以去鄉介意。

translations.literal: You should treat me as kin by affection and not let leaving your homeland weigh on your minds."
translations.idiomatic: You should treat me as kin by affection and not let leaving your homeland weigh on your minds."

sentences.zh: 」於是授襃及克、殷不害等車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed Bao, Ke, Yin Buhai, and the others General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with the Third Rank of Honor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he appointed Bao, Ke, Yin Buhai, and the others General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with the Third Rank of Honor.

sentences.zh: 常從容上席，資餼甚厚。

translations.literal: He often had them sit at ease in the upper seats and bestowed very generous provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He often had them sit at ease in the upper seats and bestowed very generous provisions.

sentences.zh: 襃等亦竝荷恩眄，忘其羈旅焉。

translations.literal: Bao and the others likewise received his gracious regard and forgot they were captives in a strange land.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and the others likewise received his gracious regard and forgot they were captives in a strange land.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，封石泉縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Bao was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiquan with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Bao was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiquan with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 世宗卽位，篤好文學。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, he was ardently fond of literature.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, he was ardently fond of literature.

sentences.zh: 時襃與庾信才名最高，特加親待。

translations.literal: At the time Bao and Yu Xin had the highest reputation for talent; they received especially close and generous treatment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Bao and Yu Xin had the highest reputation for talent; they received especially close and generous treatment.

sentences.zh: 帝每遊宴，命襃等賦詩談論，常在左右。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on excursions or banquets, he ordered Bao and the others to compose poetry and hold literary discussions, and they were constantly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on excursions or banquets, he ordered Bao and the others to compose poetry and hold literary discussions, and they were constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 尋加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was soon given the added rank of Director with the Third Rank of Honor and Opening Ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the added rank of Director with the Third Rank of Honor and Opening Ceremony.

sentences.zh: 保定中，除內史中大夫。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoding era he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖作《象經》，令襃注之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu composed the "Classic of Images" and ordered Bao to annotate it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu composed the "Classic of Images" and ordered Bao to annotate it.

sentences.zh: 引據該洽，甚見稱賞。

translations.literal: His citations were comprehensive and apt, and he was greatly praised.
translations.idiomatic: His citations were comprehensive and apt, and he was greatly praised.

sentences.zh: 襃有器局，雅識治體。

translations.literal: Bao had breadth of capacity and rightly understood the principles of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had breadth of capacity and rightly understood the principles of governance.

sentences.zh: 旣累世在江東為宰輔，高祖亦以此重之。

translations.literal: Since for generations his family had been chief ministers south of the Yangtze, Emperor Gaozu also valued him on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Since for generations his family had been chief ministers south of the Yangtze, Emperor Gaozu also valued him on that account.

sentences.zh: 建德以後，頗參朝議。

translations.literal: After the Jiande era he took part extensively in court deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiande era he took part extensively in court deliberations.

sentences.zh: 凡大詔冊，皆令襃具草。

translations.literal: Whenever there were great edicts and proclamations, Bao was ordered to draft them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there were great edicts and proclamations, Bao was ordered to draft them.

sentences.zh: 東宮旣建，授太子少保，遷小司空，仍掌綸誥。

translations.literal: After the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Junior Minister of Works, and still directed the drafting of imperial pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: After the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Junior Minister of Works, and still directed the drafting of imperial pronouncements.

sentences.zh: 乘輿行幸，襃常侍從。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went on progress, Bao often attended in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went on progress, Bao often attended in attendance.

sentences.zh: 初，襃與梁處士汝南周弘讓相善。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bao had been on good terms with the Liang recluse Zhou Hongrang of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bao had been on good terms with the Liang recluse Zhou Hongrang of Runan.

sentences.zh: 及弘讓兄弘正自陳來聘，高祖許襃等通親知音問。

translations.literal: When Hongrang's elder brother Hongzheng came from Chen on an embassy, Emperor Gaozu permitted Bao and the others to renew ties of kinship and exchange letters and inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongrang's elder brother Hongzheng came from Chen on an embassy, Emperor Gaozu permitted Bao and the others to renew ties of kinship and exchange letters and inquiries.

sentences.zh: 襃贈弘讓詩，幷致書曰：

translations.literal: Bao sent Hongrang a poem and also wrote a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: Bao sent Hongrang a poem and also wrote a letter saying:

sentences.zh: 嗣宗窮途，楊朱歧路。

translations.literal: Zong of the Ji clan at the end of the road; Yang Zhu at the crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: Like Zong of the Ji clan at the end of the road, like Yang Zhu at the crossroads.

sentences.zh: 征蓬長逝，流水不歸。

translations.literal: The expeditionary tumbleweed goes far and does not return; the flowing water does not come back.
translations.idiomatic: The expeditionary tumbleweed goes far and does not return; the flowing water does not come back.

sentences.zh: 舒慘殊方，炎涼異節，木皮春厚，桂樹冬榮。

translations.literal: Joy and sorrow differ by region; heat and cold differ by season—the bark of trees is thick in spring, the cassia tree flourishes in winter.
translations.idiomatic: Joy and sorrow differ by region; heat and cold differ by season—the bark of trees is thick in spring, the cassia tree flourishes in winter.

sentences.zh: 想攝衛惟宜，動靜多豫。

translations.literal: I trust you are taking care of yourself and that in movement and rest you have much ease.
translations.idiomatic: I trust you are taking care of yourself and that in movement and rest you have much ease.

sentences.zh: 賢兄入關，敬承款曲。

translations.literal: Your worthy elder brother has entered the Pass; I respectfully receive your warm messages.
translations.idiomatic: Your worthy elder brother has entered the Pass; I respectfully receive your warm messages.

sentences.zh: 猶依杜陵之水，尚保池陽之田，鏟跡幽蹊，銷聲穹谷。

translations.literal: You still keep to the waters of the Du mound and still preserve the fields of Chiyang, effacing your tracks on hidden paths and silencing your name in lofty valleys.
translations.idiomatic: You still keep to the waters of the Du mound and still preserve the fields of Chiyang, effacing your tracks on hidden paths and silencing your name in lofty valleys.

sentences.zh: 何期愉樂，幸甚！

translations.literal: Who would have expected such pleasure—how fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: Who would have expected such pleasure—how fortunate!

sentences.zh: 幸甚！

translations.literal: How fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: How fortunate!

sentences.zh: 弟昔因多疾，亟覽九仙之方；

translations.literal: Your younger brother formerly, because of many illnesses, eagerly studied the recipes of the Nine Immortals;
translations.idiomatic: Your younger brother formerly, because of many illnesses, eagerly studied the recipes of the Nine Immortals;

sentences.zh: 晚涉世途，常懷五嶽之舉。

translations.literal: later he entered the world's road and constantly cherished the wish to climb the Five Peaks.
translations.idiomatic: later he entered the world's road and constantly cherished the wish to climb the Five Peaks.

sentences.zh: 同夫關令，物色異人；

translations.literal: Like the Pass Keeper, he sought out extraordinary men;
translations.idiomatic: Like the Pass Keeper, he sought out extraordinary men;

sentences.zh: 譬彼客卿，服膺高士。

translations.literal: like that guest minister, he took to heart lofty gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: like that guest minister, he took to heart lofty gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 上經說道，屢聽玄牝之談；

translations.literal: In the upper classic he heard discourse on the Way and often listened to talks on the mysterious female;
translations.idiomatic: In the upper classic he heard discourse on the Way and often listened to talks on the mysterious female;

sentences.zh: 中藥養神，每稟丹沙之說。

translations.literal: in the middle he nourished the spirit with medicine and often received instruction on cinnabar sand.
translations.idiomatic: in the middle he nourished the spirit with medicine and often received instruction on cinnabar sand.

sentences.zh: 頃年事遒盡，容發衰謝，芸其黃矣，零落無時。

translations.literal: In recent years affairs have pressed hard to the end; my hair and face have declined and withered—the plant is yellowing and will fall without season.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years affairs have pressed hard to the end; my hair and face have declined and withered—the plant is yellowing and will fall without season.

sentences.zh: 還念生涯，繁憂總集。

translations.literal: Turning back to consider my life, anxious cares gather in full.
translations.idiomatic: Turning back to consider my life, anxious cares gather in full.

sentences.zh: 視陰愒日，猶趙孟之徂年；

translations.literal: Watching the shade and fearing the sun, like Zhao Meng's sense of the years passing;
translations.idiomatic: Watching the shade and fearing the sun, like Zhao Meng's sense of the years passing;

sentences.zh: 負杖行吟，同劉琨之積慘。

translations.literal: Leaning on his staff and walking while chanting, like Liu Kun's accumulated grief.
translations.idiomatic: Leaning on his staff and walking while chanting, like Liu Kun's accumulated grief.

sentences.zh: 河陽北臨，空思鞏縣；

translations.literal: North of Heyang I look out in vain, thinking of Gong county;
translations.idiomatic: North of Heyang I look out in vain, thinking of Gong county;

sentences.zh: 霸陵南望，還見長安。

translations.literal: Gazing south from Baling, I still see Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing south from Baling, I still see Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 所冀書生之魂，來依舊壤；

translations.literal: I hope the scholar's soul may come to rest on its old soil;
translations.idiomatic: I hope the scholar's soul may come to rest on its old soil;

sentences.zh: 射聲之鬼，無恨他鄉。

translations.literal: and that the ghost of the Archers' Office may have no regret in a strange land.
translations.idiomatic: and that the ghost of the Archers' Office may have no regret in a strange land.

sentences.zh: 白雲在天，長離別矣，會見之期，邈無日矣。

translations.literal: White clouds are in the sky; long is this parting; the day of meeting is far off and has no date.
translations.idiomatic: White clouds are in the sky; long is this parting; the day of meeting is far off and has no date.

sentences.zh: 援筆攬紙，龍鍾橫集。

translations.literal: Taking up the brush and gathering paper, decrepitude crowds in from every side.
translations.idiomatic: Taking up the brush and gathering paper, decrepitude crowds in from every side.

sentences.zh: 弘讓復書曰：

translations.literal: Hongrang wrote back in reply:
translations.idiomatic: Hongrang wrote back in reply:

sentences.zh: 甚矣悲哉！

translations.literal: How very sad! How very sad!
translations.idiomatic: How very sad! How very sad!

sentences.zh: 此之為別也。

translations.literal: Such is this parting.
translations.idiomatic: Such is this parting.

sentences.zh: 雲飛泥沉，金鑠蘭滅，玉音不嗣，瑤華莫因。

translations.literal: Clouds fly and mud sinks; gold melts and orchids perish; jade tones are not continued; jade blossoms are not renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds fly and mud sinks; gold melts and orchids perish; jade tones are not continued; jade blossoms are not renewed.

sentences.zh: 家兄至自鎬京，致書於穹穀。

translations.literal: My elder brother has come from Haojing and sent a letter to the lofty valley.
translations.idiomatic: My elder brother has come from Haojing and sent a letter to the lofty valley.

sentences.zh: 故人之跡，有如對面，開題申紙，流臉沾膝。

translations.literal: The traces of an old friend are as though face to face; opening the letter and spreading the paper, tears stream down and soak the knees.
translations.idiomatic: The traces of an old friend are as though face to face; opening the letter and spreading the paper, tears stream down and soak the knees.

sentences.zh: 江南燠熱，橘柚冬青；

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze it is sultry and hot; oranges and pomelos are green in winter;
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze it is sultry and hot; oranges and pomelos are green in winter;

sentences.zh: 渭北冱寒，楊榆晚葉。

translations.literal: north of the Wei it is bitterly cold; poplars and elms shed their leaves late.
translations.idiomatic: north of the Wei it is bitterly cold; poplars and elms shed their leaves late.

sentences.zh: 土風氣候，各集所安，餐衛適時，寢興多福。

translations.literal: Local custom and climate each gather where men are at ease; food and care suit the season—may your rest and rising bring much good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom and climate each gather where men are at ease; food and care suit the season—may your rest and rising bring much good fortune.

sentences.zh: 甚善！

translations.literal: Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Excellent!

sentences.zh: 甚善！

translations.literal: Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Excellent!

sentences.zh: 與弟分袂西陝，言反東區，雖保周陵，還依蔣徑，三薑離楩，二仲不歸。

translations.literal: When I parted from you at West Shaanxi, I spoke of returning to the eastern districts; though I kept to the Zhou tombs, I would still rely on the Jiang path—the three Jiangs left the catalpa, and the two Zhongs did not return.
translations.idiomatic: When I parted from you at West Shaanxi, I spoke of returning to the eastern districts; though I kept to the Zhou tombs, I would still rely on the Jiang path—the three Jiangs left the catalpa, and the two Zhongs did not return.

sentences.zh: 糜鹿為曹，更多悲緒。

translations.literal: Elk and deer form their herds, and sorrowful feelings grow all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Elk and deer form their herds, and sorrowful feelings grow all the more.

sentences.zh: 丹經在握，貧病莫諧；

translations.literal: The cinnabar classic is in hand, yet poverty and illness cannot be harmonized;
translations.idiomatic: The cinnabar classic is in hand, yet poverty and illness cannot be harmonized;

sentences.zh: 芝術可求，恆為采掇。

translations.literal: glossy ganoderma and atractylodes may be sought and are constantly gathered.
translations.idiomatic: glossy ganoderma and atractylodes may be sought and are constantly gathered.

sentences.zh: 昔吾壯日，及弟富年，俱值邕熙，竝歡衡泌。

translations.literal: In former days in our vigorous years, when you too were in your rich prime, we both met a time of brightness and rejoiced together in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: In former days in our vigorous years, when you too were in your rich prime, we both met a time of brightness and rejoiced together in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 南風雅操，清商妙曲，弦琴促坐，無乏名晨。

translations.literal: Southern airs and elegant melodies, pure Shang and marvelous tunes—zithers and lutes at close seats, never lacking famous mornings.
translations.idiomatic: Southern airs and elegant melodies, pure Shang and marvelous tunes—zithers and lutes at close seats, never lacking famous mornings.

sentences.zh: 玉瀝金華，冀獲難老。

translations.literal: Jade dew and golden splendor—we hoped to attain difficult old age.
translations.idiomatic: Jade dew and golden splendor—we hoped to attain difficult old age.

sentences.zh: 不虞一旦，翻覆波瀾。

translations.literal: We did not expect that in a single morning waves would overturn.
translations.idiomatic: We did not expect that in a single morning waves would overturn.

sentences.zh: 吾已愒陰，弟非茂齒。

translations.literal: I have already wearied of shade; you are not in your flourishing years.
translations.idiomatic: I have already wearied of shade; you are not in your flourishing years.

sentences.zh: 禽、尚之契，各在天涯，永念生平，難為胸臆。

translations.literal: The bond of Qin and Shang each lies at the ends of heaven; ever remembering our lives together, it is hard to bear in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: The bond of Qin and Shang each lies at the ends of heaven; ever remembering our lives together, it is hard to bear in the breast.

sentences.zh: 且當視陰數箭，排愁破涕。

translations.literal: For now you should watch the shade and count the arrows, drive off sorrow and break into tears.
translations.idiomatic: For now you should watch the shade and count the arrows, drive off sorrow and break into tears.

sentences.zh: 人生樂耳，憂戚何為。

translations.literal: Human life is joy; what is sorrow for?
translations.idiomatic: Human life is joy; what is sorrow for?

sentences.zh: 豈能遽悲次房，遊魂不反。

translations.literal: How could one suddenly grieve for Cifang, whose wandering soul does not return?
translations.idiomatic: How could one suddenly grieve for Cifang, whose wandering soul does not return?

sentences.zh: 遠〔傷金〕

translations.literal: Far off — grieving for Jin (damaged passage).
translations.idiomatic: Far away he grieved for Jin; the text here is damaged in the manuscript.

translations.literal: (Chan)
translations.idiomatic: (Chan)

sentences.zh: 〔彥〕，骸柩無托。

translations.literal: [Yan], with no coffin to receive the bones.
translations.idiomatic: [Yan], with no coffin to receive the bones.

sentences.zh: 但願愛玉體，珍金箱，保期頤，享黃發。

translations.literal: I only wish you would cherish your jade body and treasure your golden casket, preserve your years of ease, and enjoy white hair.
translations.idiomatic: I only wish you would cherish your jade body and treasure your golden casket, preserve your years of ease, and enjoy white hair.

sentences.zh: 猶冀蒼

translations.literal: I still hope the azure
translations.idiomatic: I still hope the azure

translations.literal: (Ying)
translations.idiomatic: (Ying)

sentences.zh: 〔雁〕頳鯉，時傳尺素，清風朗月，俱寄相思。

translations.literal: [wild goose] and the red carp may from time to time convey a letter; clear wind and bright moon—all bear my longing.
translations.idiomatic: [wild goose] and the red carp may from time to time convey a letter; clear wind and bright moon—all bear my longing.

sentences.zh: 子淵，子淵，長為別矣！

translations.literal: Ziyuan, Ziyuan—long is this parting!
translations.idiomatic: Ziyuan, Ziyuan—long is this parting!

sentences.zh: 握管操觚，聲淚俱咽。

translations.literal: Grasping the tube and holding the writing tablet, voice and tears alike choke.
translations.idiomatic: Grasping the tube and holding the writing tablet, voice and tears alike choke.

sentences.zh: 尋出為

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went out as
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he went out as

translations.literal: (Xuan)
translations.idiomatic: (Xuan)

sentences.zh: 〔宜〕州刺史。

translations.literal: [Yi] provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: [Yi] provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 卒於位，時年六十四。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 子鼒嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zi inherited.

sentences.zh: 庾信字子山，南陽新野人也。

translations.literal: Yu Xin, courtesy name Zishan, was a native of Xinye in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xin, styled Zishan, came from Xinye in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖易，齊徵士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi was a Qi Recluse Summoned.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi was a Qi Recluse Summoned.

sentences.zh: 父肩吾，梁散騎常侍、中書令。

translations.literal: His father Jianwu was Liang Attendant Cavalier at Large and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jianwu was Liang Attendant Cavalier at Large and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 信幼而俊邁，聰敏絕倫。

translations.literal: From youth Xin was lofty and surpassing, with intelligence beyond his peers.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xin was lofty and surpassing, with intelligence beyond his peers.

sentences.zh: 博覽羣書，尤善《春秋左氏傳》。

translations.literal: He read widely among the classics and was especially skilled in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely among the classics and was especially skilled in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，腰帶十圍，容止頹然，有過人者。

translations.literal: He was eight feet in height, his belt ten spans around; his bearing and deportment were striking, with qualities surpassing other men.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet tall, with a belt ten spans around; his bearing was striking and surpassed other men.

sentences.zh: 起家湘東國常侍，轉安南府參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as Regular Attendant of the Kingdom of Xiangdong and was transferred to Aide of the An'nan headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Regular Attendant of the Kingdom of Xiangdong and was transferred to Aide of the An'nan headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時肩吾為梁太子中庶子，掌管記。

translations.literal: At the time Jianwu was Liang Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and directed the secretariat records.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jianwu was Liang Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and directed the secretariat records.

sentences.zh: 東海徐摛為左衛率。

translations.literal: Xu Ling of Donghai was Left Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling of Donghai was Left Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 摛子陵及信，竝為抄撰學士。

translations.literal: Ling's son Ling and Xin were both Copying and Compiling Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's son Ling and Xin were both Copying and Compiling Academicians.

sentences.zh: 父子在東宮，出入禁闥，恩禮莫與比靈斯。

translations.literal: Father and son were in the Eastern Palace, entering and leaving the forbidden gates; in favor and ceremony none could compare with them.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were in the Eastern Palace, entering and leaving the forbidden gates; in favor and ceremony none could compare with them.

sentences.zh: 旣有盛才，文竝綺豔，故世號為徐、庾體焉。

translations.literal: Since both had outstanding talent and their writings were alike ornate and brilliant, the age therefore called it the Xu–Yu style.
translations.idiomatic: Since both had outstanding talent and their writings were alike ornate and brilliant, the age therefore called it the Xu–Yu style.

sentences.zh: 當時後進，競相模範。

translations.literal: The younger men of the time all took them as models in competition.
translations.idiomatic: The younger men of the time all took them as models in competition.

sentences.zh: 每有一文，京都莫不傳誦。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a new piece of writing, the capital had none who did not pass it around and chant it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there was a new piece of writing, the capital had none who did not pass it around and chant it.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書度支郎中、通直正員郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Director of the Bureau of Revenue in the Ministry of Works and Regular Attendant of the Direct Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Director of the Bureau of Revenue in the Ministry of Works and Regular Attendant of the Direct Office.

sentences.zh: 出為郢州別駕。

translations.literal: He went out to be Vice Administrator of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to be Vice Administrator of Ying province.

sentences.zh: 尋兼通直散騎常侍，聘于東魏。

translations.literal: He was soon given the added post of Attendant Cavalier at Large of the Direct Office and was sent on embassy to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the added post of Attendant Cavalier at Large of the Direct Office and was sent on embassy to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 文章辭令，盛為鄴下所稱。

translations.literal: His literary compositions and diplomatic language were greatly praised below Ye.
translations.idiomatic: His literary compositions and diplomatic language were greatly praised below Ye.

sentences.zh: 還為東宮學士，領建康令。

translations.literal: On his return he became an Eastern Palace academician and concurrently Magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became an Eastern Palace academician and concurrently Magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 侯景作亂，梁簡文帝命信率宮中文武千餘人，營於朱雀航。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing raised rebellion, Emperor Jianwen of Liang ordered Xin to lead more than a thousand civil and military officials of the palace in encamping at the Zhuque ford.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing raised rebellion, Emperor Jianwen of Liang ordered Xin to lead more than a thousand civil and military officials of the palace in encamping at the Zhuque ford.

sentences.zh: 及景至，信以衆先退。

translations.literal: When Jing arrived, Xin led the troops in retreating first.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing arrived, Xin led the troops in retreating first.

sentences.zh: 臺城陷後，信奔于江陵。

translations.literal: After the terrace city fell, Xin fled to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: After the terrace city fell, Xin fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制，除御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the provisional regency, Xin was appointed Imperial Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the provisional regency, Xin was appointed Imperial Secretary.

sentences.zh: 及卽位，轉右衛將軍，封武康縣侯，加散騎常侍，來聘於我。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, Xin was transferred to General of the Right Guards, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wukang, and given the added rank of Attendant Cavalier at Large; he came on embassy to our court.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne, Xin was transferred to General of the Right Guards, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wukang, and given the added rank of Attendant Cavalier at Large; he came on embassy to our court.

sentences.zh: 屬大軍南討，遂留長安。

translations.literal: Just then the great army marched south to attack, and he therefore remained at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the great army marched south to attack, and he therefore remained at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，拜使持節、撫軍將軍、右金紫光祿大夫、大都督，尋進車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the Army, Household Counsellor with the Right of Golden Bells and Purple Pendants, and Chief Commander; he was soon promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with the Third Rank of Honor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling was pacified, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the Army, Household Counsellor with the Right of Golden Bells and Purple Pendants, and Chief Commander; he was soon promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with the Third Rank of Honor.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，封臨清縣子，邑五百戶，除司水下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Xin was enfeoffed as Viscount of Linqing with a fief of five hundred households and appointed Grand Master of the Bureau of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Xin was enfeoffed as Viscount of Linqing with a fief of five hundred households and appointed Grand Master of the Bureau of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 出為弘農郡守，遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、司憲中大夫，進爵義城縣侯。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Hongnong commandery, was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry, Director with the Third Rank of Honor and Opening Ceremony, and Grand Master of the Bureau of Justice, and was advanced in rank to Marquis of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Administrator of Hongnong commandery, was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry, Director with the Third Rank of Honor and Opening Ceremony, and Grand Master of the Bureau of Justice, and was advanced in rank to Marquis of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 俄拜洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Governor of Luo province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Governor of Luo province.

sentences.zh: 信多識舊章，為政簡靜，吏民安之。

translations.literal: Xin knew many old regulations; his governance was simple and quiet, and officials and people were at ease under him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin knew many old regulations; his governance was simple and quiet, and officials and people were at ease under him.

sentences.zh: 時陳氏與朝廷通好，南北流寓之士，各許還其舊國。

translations.literal: At the time Chen was on friendly terms with the court, and scholars stranded north and south were each permitted to return to their former states.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chen was on friendly terms with the court, and scholars stranded north and south were each permitted to return to their former states.

sentences.zh: 陳氏乃請王襃及信等十數人。

translations.literal: Chen therefore requested Wang Bao and Xin and more than ten others.
translations.idiomatic: Chen therefore requested Wang Bao and Xin and more than ten others.

sentences.zh: 高祖唯放王克、殷不害等，信及襃竝留而不遣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu released only Wang Ke, Yin Buhai, and the like; Xin and Bao were both detained and not sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu released only Wang Ke, Yin Buhai, and the like; Xin and Bao were both detained and not sent away.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為司宗中大夫。

translations.literal: He was soon summoned to be Grand Master of the Bureau of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to be Grand Master of the Bureau of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 世宗、高祖竝雅好文學，信特蒙恩禮。

translations.literal: Emperors Shizong and Gaozu were both fond of literature, and Xin received special favor and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Shizong and Gaozu were both fond of literature, and Xin received special favor and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 至於趙、滕諸王，周旋款至，有若布衣之交。

translations.literal: As for the princes Zhao, Teng, and the rest, they treated him with intimate courtesy, as though he were a friend in plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: As for the princes Zhao, Teng, and the rest, they treated him with intimate courtesy, as though he were a friend in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 羣公碑誌，多相請託。

translations.idiomatic: The dukes and lords, for their stele inscriptions and dirges, largely entrusted him with the writing.

translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Bao was quite on a par with Xin; among the remaining literary men, none could reach them.

translations.idiomatic: Though Xin's rank and position were eminent and manifest, he often had thoughts of his home district.

translations.idiomatic: In the year wuchen, in the month jianhai, the great robber shifted the state and Jinling collapsed.

sentences.zh: 余乃竄身荒谷，公私塗炭。

translations.literal: I then hid myself in a desolate valley; public and private alike were trampled in the mire.
translations.idiomatic: I then hid myself in a desolate valley; public and private alike were trampled in the mire.

sentences.zh: 華陽奔命，有去無歸，中興道消，窮於甲戌。

translations.literal: At Huayang I fled for my life—there was going but no returning; the way of restoration vanished and came to an end in jiaxu.
translations.idiomatic: At Huayang I fled for my life—there was going but no returning; the way of restoration vanished and came to an end in jiaxu.

sentences.zh: 三日哭於都亭，三年囚於別館。

translations.literal: For three days I wept at the capital pavilion; for three years I was a prisoner in the guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: For three days I wept at the capital pavilion; for three years I was a prisoner in the guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 天道周星，物極不反。

translations.literal: Heaven's way revolves through the stars; when things reach their limit they do not turn back.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way revolves through the stars; when things reach their limit they do not turn back.

sentences.zh: 傅燮之但悲身世，無所求生；

translations.literal: Fu Xie only grieved for his person and age and sought nothing to live for;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xie only grieved for his person and age and sought nothing to live for;

sentences.zh: 袁安之每念王室，自然流涕。

translations.literal: Yuan An, whenever he thought of the royal house, naturally shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan An, whenever he thought of the royal house, naturally shed tears.

sentences.zh: 昔桓君山之志事，杜元凱之生平，竝有著書，咸能自序。

translations.literal: Formerly the ambitions and affairs of Lord Mountain Huan and the life of Du Yuankai—both wrote books and could each set forth their own accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the ambitions and affairs of Lord Mountain Huan and the life of Du Yuankai—both wrote books and could each set forth their own accounts.

sentences.zh: 潘岳之文彩，始述家風；

translations.literal: The literary splendor of Pan Yue first described his family style;
translations.idiomatic: The literary splendor of Pan Yue first described his family style;

translations.literal: the fu and poems of Lu Ji largely set forth the virtue of his age.
translations.idiomatic: the fu and poems of Lu Ji largely set forth the virtue of his age.

sentences.zh: 信年始二毛，卽逢喪亂，藐是流離，至于暮齒。

translations.literal: When Xin was barely twenty he met with disorder and ruin; trifling was this wandering exile, down to old age.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin was barely twenty he met with disorder and ruin; trifling was this wandering exile, down to old age.

sentences.zh: 《燕謌》遠別，悲不自勝；

translations.literal: "Song of the Yan" was a distant parting, and grief could not master itself;
translations.idiomatic: "Song of the Yan" was a distant parting, and grief could not master itself;

sentences.zh: 楚老相逢，泣將何及。

translations.literal: when old men of Chu meet, what tears are left to shed?
translations.idiomatic: when old men of Chu meet, what tears are left to shed?

sentences.zh: 畏南山之雨，忽踐秦庭；

translations.literal: I feared the rain on the southern mountains, then suddenly trod the Qin court;
translations.idiomatic: I feared the rain on the southern mountains, then suddenly trod the Qin court;

translations.literal: yielded the shore of the eastern sea and then ate the Zhou millet.
translations.idiomatic: yielded the shore of the eastern sea and then ate the Zhou millet.

sentences.zh: 下亭漂泊，皋橋羈旅，楚歌非取樂之方，魯酒無忘憂之用。

translations.literal: At Xiating I drifted in exile; at Gaoqiao I lodged as a captive—Chu songs were no way to take joy, and Lu wine had no power to banish grief.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiading I drifted in exile; at Gaoqiao I lodged as a captive—Chu songs were no way to take joy, and Lu wine had no power to banish grief.

translations.idiomatic: The sun sets and the road is far—what age is this among men?

translations.literal: the brave warrior does not return; the cold wind is bleak.
translations.idiomatic: the brave warrior does not return; the cold wind is bleak.

translations.idiomatic: Bian He gazed at the pillar; he received the linked cities yet was deceived;

translations.literal: Shen Baoxu beat his head upon the ground until it broke;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baoxu beat his head upon the ground until it broke;

translations.literal: Duke Ai of Cai wept until his tears were exhausted, and blood was added thereto.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ai of Cai wept until his tears were exhausted, and blood was added thereto.

translations.literal: Willows moved on the angling terrace—not to be looked for from Jade Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Willows moved on the angling terrace—not to be looked for from Jade Gate;

translations.literal: cranes cried at Huating—how could the He Bridge be heard?
translations.idiomatic: cranes cried at Huating—how could the He Bridge be heard?

translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce took the realm as three parts and commanded but one brigade;

translations.literal: Xiang Yu used the youths of Jiangdong—only eight thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu used the youths of Jiangdong—only eight thousand men.

translations.literal: Thereupon they split mountains and rivers and carved up the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they split mountains and rivers and carved up the realm.

sentences.zh: 豈有百萬義師，一朝卷甲，芟夷斬伐，如草木焉。

translations.literal: Could a million righteous armies in one morning roll up their armor and be mowed down and hewn like grass and trees?
translations.idiomatic: Could a million righteous armies in one morning roll up their armor and be mowed down and hewn like grass and trees?

translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze and Huai had no barrier of shore; pavilion walls had no hedge of fence.

translations.literal: Those who met with heads and gathered with winnowing baskets united in vertical-horizontal alliances;
translations.idiomatic: Those who met with heads and gathered with winnowing baskets united in vertical-horizontal alliances;

translations.literal: those with hoes and briers and thorn-staves took advantage and seized the moment.
translations.idiomatic: those with hoes and briers and thorn-staves took advantage and seized the moment.

translations.idiomatic: Could it be that the royal qi south of the Yangtze was fated to end after three hundred years?

translations.idiomatic: Alas!

translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent and human affairs—things that can rend the heart with sorrow.

translations.idiomatic: wind and storm block the way; Penglai has no date when one may arrive.

translations.idiomatic: The exhausted wish to express their words; the weary must sing their affairs.

translations.idiomatic: Lu Shiheng heard it and clapped his hands—this was what he would willingly accept;

translations.idiomatic: It dwelt facing the Luo with weight of generations; its town overlooked the river in tranquil security.

translations.idiomatic: When the hardships of Yongjia came, the Central Plain first lacked a lord.

translations.idiomatic: The people leaned on walls for pillows; roads were crossed by wolves and tigers.

translations.idiomatic: They built a state crossing the Yangtze; we were cast out with our ancestors.

translations.idiomatic: Nanyang was divided and fields granted; the eastern march was split and soil enfeoffed.

translations.idiomatic: Thatched huts were cut at Song Yu's dwelling; paths were bored through the mansion by the river.

translations.idiomatic: Wood and water alternated in their cycles; mountains and rivers collapsed and dried up.

translations.literal: The family had the straight Way; many preserved their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The family had the straight Way; many preserved their integrity.

translations.idiomatic: Training sons showed pure depth; serving the ruler displayed righteous fervor.

translations.idiomatic: In Xinye there was a shrine of living sacrifice; in Henan there was a stele of barbarian script.

translations.literal: Moreover there was the recluse of Shaowei, the withdrawn man of Tianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover there was the recluse of Shaowei, the withdrawn man of Tianshan.

translations.idiomatic: The steps and courtyard were an empty valley; at gate and lane stood wagons of rushes.

translations.idiomatic: Talk moved to the lecturing tree; one approached the bamboo of brief writings.

translations.literal: Descent brought forth the virtue of the age; birth bore forth the loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Descent brought forth the virtue of the age; birth bore forth the loyal minister.

translations.idiomatic: Literary words rose above the Jia Observatory; models flourished on the banks of Zhang.

translations.idiomatic: Alas, there was the Way but no phoenix; one sighed that it was not the time, yet there was a unicorn.

translations.idiomatic: In the year the prince was at the Luo ford, in the year Lancheng shot for office, he first held incense at Jianli and still spread his wings at Chongxian.

translations.idiomatic: He wandered the lecture hall of accumulated thunder and took his place among the bright departing caps; having tilted the gourd he drank the sea, he then measured the tube to peer at heaven.

translations.literal: The square pond's water was white; the angling islet's pool was round.
translations.idiomatic: The square pond's water was white; the angling islet's pool was round.

translations.idiomatic: He attended military plans in the martial tent and listened to elegant melodies on the literary strings.

translations.literal: Then he removed his suspension and entered the registry; he honored literature and joined with martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Then he removed his suspension and entered the registry; he honored literature and joined with martial affairs.

translations.literal: He dwelt in the imperial carriage district and commanded troops; he went out from Orchid Pool and directed the noon office.
translations.idiomatic: He dwelt in the imperial carriage district and commanded troops; he went out from Orchid Pool and directed the noon office.

translations.idiomatic: He discussed warfare with the lord of the Yangtze and Han and wiped the jade tablet for the master of Xihe.

translations.literal: At that time court and countryside rejoiced; pools and terraces sounded bells and drums.
translations.idiomatic: At that time court and countryside rejoiced; pools and terraces sounded bells and drums.

sentences.zh: 里為冠蓋，門成鄒魯。

translations.literal: Within the lanes were caps and canopies; at the gates stood men of Zou and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Within the lanes were caps and canopies; at the gates stood men of Zou and Lu.

sentences.zh: 連茂苑於海陵，跨橫塘於江浦。

translations.idiomatic: The luxuriant park was joined to Hailing; the cross embankment spanned the river mouth.

translations.idiomatic: At the eastern gate stone was whipped into a bridge; at the southern extremity bronze was cast into pillars.
